title: Web Administrators
description: Manage web environment design, deployment, development and maintenance activities. Perform testing and quality assurance of web sites and web applications.

tasks.text: Monitor systems for intrusions or denial of service attacks, and report security breaches to appropriate personnel.
Test issues such as system integration, performance, and system security on a regular schedule or after any major program modifications.
Check and analyze operating system or application log files regularly to verify proper system performance.
Test new software packages for use in Web operations or other applications.
Identify or document backup or recovery plans.
Back up or modify applications and related data to provide for disaster recovery.
Perform user testing or usage analyses to determine Web sites' effectiveness or usability.
Track, compile, and analyze Web site usage data.
Test backup or recovery plans regularly and resolve any problems.
Gather, analyze, or document user feedback to locate or resolve sources of problems.
Set up or maintain monitoring tools on Web servers or Web sites.
Monitor Web developments through continuing education, reading, or participation in professional conferences, workshops, or groups.
Identify or address interoperability requirements.
Develop and implement marketing plans for home pages, including print advertising or advertisement rotation.
Evaluate or recommend server hardware or software.
Correct testing-identified problems, or recommend actions for their resolution.
Identify, standardize, and communicate levels of access and security.
Determine sources of Web page or server problems, and take action to correct such problems.
Implement updates, upgrades, and patches in a timely manner to limit loss of service.
Implement Web site security measures, such as firewalls or message encryption.
Document application and Web site changes or change procedures.
Review or update Web page content or links in a timely manner, using appropriate tools.
Install or configure Web server software or hardware to ensure that directory structure is well-defined, logical, and secure, and that files are named properly.
Administer internet or intranet infrastructure, including Web, file, and mail servers.
Develop or document style guidelines for Web site content.
Develop Web site performance metrics.
Develop or implement procedures for ongoing Web site revision.
Evaluate testing routines or procedures for adequacy, sufficiency, and effectiveness.
Document installation or configuration procedures to allow maintenance and repetition.
Develop testing routines and procedures.
Collaborate with development teams to discuss, analyze, or resolve usability issues.
Recommend Web site improvements, and develop budgets to support recommendations.
Collaborate with Web developers to create and operate internal and external Web sites, or to manage projects, such as e-marketing campaigns.
Provide training or technical assistance in Web site implementation or use.
Inform Web site users of problems, problem resolutions, or application changes and updates.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Programming
skills.def: Writing computer programs for various purposes.

skills.name: Quality Control Analysis
skills.def: Conducting tests and inspections of products, services, or processes to evaluate quality or performance.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Operations Analysis
skills.def: Analyzing needs and product requirements to create a design.

skills.name: Web platform development software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications accessed through web sites or using web technologies such as HTML. Examples: Adobe ColdFusion, AJAX, Apache Struts, Apache Tomcat.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Amazon Web Services AWS software, Microsoft Access, Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL.

skills.name: Transaction server software
skills.def: Software to isolate business logic in programs from platform-specific code, so each can be maintained independently. May provide transaction management, clustering, failover, or load balancing. Examples: Customer information control system CICS, IBM Middleware, Microsoft Internet Information Services (IIS), Microsoft Internet Information Services (IIS) Manager.

skills.name: Development environment software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications which run on a computer or mobile device. Examples: Adobe ActionScript, Apache Ant, Microsoft .NET Framework, Microsoft Azure software.

skills.name: Web page creation and editing software
skills.def: Software to develop or edit web sites or individual pages. Examples: Adobe Dreamweaver, Adobe Experience Manager (AEM), Adobe Macromedia HomeSite, Content management systems CMS.

skills.name: Object or component oriented development software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications using object-oriented programming concepts. Examples: Embarcadero Delphi, Microsoft ActiveX, Oracle Java, Perl.
